title: The morning a second sun lit up Russia ☄️
subject: meteor
description:
Would you have run to the window too? 👇

On February 15, 2013, an undetected 60-foot asteroid exploded over Chelyabinsk, Russia, briefly outshining the Sun. Its shockwave damaged about 7,200 buildings and injured 1,491 people.

Sources: Wikipedia, "Chelyabinsk meteor"; The Planetary Society, "What was the Chelyabinsk meteor event?"; Space.com, "Russian Meteor Explosion Outshone Sun" (Feb 15, 2013, quoting NASA JPL's Paul Chodas).

scenes.text: At 9:20 one morning, a second sun rose over Russia.
Chelyabinsk, February 15, 2013. A 60-foot asteroid hit the air at 42,000 mph. Nobody had spotted it.
It blew apart 18 miles up with about 30 times the energy of the Hiroshima bomb.
People rushed to their windows. The shockwave hit nearly 3 minutes later.
Glass blew in across 7,200 buildings, and 1,491 people were hurt.
Teacher Yulia Karbysheva had her 44 students duck and cover. She was badly cut. None of them were.
